title: Streaming histogram aggregator for per-tenant latency and token-cost KPIs
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Problem: Per-request latency and per-token cost measurements are currently emitted as high-cardinality point metrics from many edge producers, resulting in ingestion costs, unbounded label cardinality, and slow SLO queries. We need a streaming pre-aggregation component that compacts raw inference KPIs into deterministic histogram envelopes per tenant/route/model with trace-exemplar linkage and OTLP/Prometheus compatible outputs.

Scope: Implement a sidecar/ingest-stage aggregator that consumes OTLP/Prom traces/metrics and raw KPI events, maintains bounded streaming histograms (HDR or t-digest variant), emits periodic histogram windows and exemplars, and forwards summaries to the central metrics mesh and Prometheus remote_write. Ensure per-tenant isolation, label whitelisting, and trace linkage for latency debugging.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Aggregator emits Prometheus-compatible histogram_metric with stable bucket boundaries and exemplar trace IDs for >95% of slow-sample events.
2) End-to-end ingested metric points reduced by >=70% for high-cardinality tenants during synthetic load test.
3) SLO queries (p50/p95/p99) computed from aggregated histograms differ from raw-sampled queries by <=5% in controlled replay.
4) No cross-tenant label leakage in aggregation outputs.
5) Unit and integration tests + load test harness completed and green.
technical_notes:
Design choices: use compact HDR histogram representation for bucketed export; keep internal sketch precision tunable per-cycle (default: 3 significant digits). Deterministic bucket boundaries derived from global config so rollups from multiple shards merge cleanly. Memory caps per-tenant via reservoir sampling for extreme churn. Exemplar attachment: attach trace_id/span_id and model_route meta to exemplar labels; ensure exemplar size bounded. Export formats: OTLP metrics (histogram) + Prometheus remote_write with histogram family. Backfill path: dual-writing raw points and aggregated histograms during canary.
Libraries: libhdr (C++ sidecar) or gohdr for collector; proto: OTLP v1 histogram, prometheus exposition v0.0.4.
Edge cases: single-sample windows must still emit a valid histogram (min bucket).
Observability: add internal metrics for aggregator memory, flush latency, dropped_samples by tenant.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 - Prototype (2 wks): sidecar that consumes synthetic event stream, produces deterministic HDR histogram windows, attach trace exemplar. Phase 2 - Integration (2 wks): wire into metric mesh accepting OTLP histograms and Prom remote_write; add label whitelist config and tenant quotas. Phase 3 - Hardening (1 wk): production tests, metrics for aggregator health, OOM prevention. Phase 4 - Canary rollout (2 wks): roll to 5% of tenants, compare SLO calc accuracy and ingestion delta, then ramp.

Key tasks: implement bucket engine, per-tenant state eviction, exemplar exporter, config UI for bucket precision and flush interval, add RBAC to control which tenants enable aggregation.
progress_log: 2026-03-10 - Ticket created by Aisha: sketched problem statement and goals.
2026-03-11 - Design sync with Observability and Runtime: agreed on HDR-based histograms and deterministic buckets.
2026-03-12 - Spike: prototype sidecar that reads newline JSON events and outputs histogram proto; early results show 75% point reduction at 10k qps.
2026-03-13 - Security review kickoff: confirmed no plaintext PII in metrics; exemplar payload limited to trace/span ids and model_route.
2026-03-14 - Assignee Miguel implemented merge logic for same-bucket histograms across shards; integration tests added to CI.
2026-03-14 - Next: add label whitelist and per-tenant memory cap, finalize export format with Prometheus team.
testing_plan: Unit tests for histogram merging and exemplar attachment. Integration tests that run sidecar + remote_write in docker-compose with mock Prometheus receiver. E2E synthetic load: replay 100M events across 100 tenants at 20k qps and validate ingestion reduction and SLO accuracy. Fault injection: simulate OOM, disk backpressure, and OTLP export failures to ensure safe degradation (fallback to sampling).
rollout_plan: 1) Canary 5% tenants with dual-write (raw + aggregated) for 2 weeks. 2) Monitor comparison dashboards for SLO drift, exemplar coverage, ingestion delta. 3) If metrics stable, ramp to 25% then 100% over successive cycles. 4) Provide opt-out toggle per-tenant and runtime override for emergency rollback.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Cardinality explosion from unvetted labels -> Mitigation: enforce label whitelist and collapse unknown label values to __redacted__. Risk: Aggregation bugs cause SLO misestimation -> Mitigation: dual-write during canary and assert queries against raw sample. Risk: Memory blowup for noisy tenants -> Mitigation: per-tenant memory cap and LRU eviction with telemetry. Risk: Exemplars not present for slow tails -> Mitigation: deterministic slow-sample capture policy and fallback sampling by trace rate.
notes_for_reviewers: Focus reviews on: correctness of bucket merge semantics across shards, exemplar payload privacy constraints, and memory safety of the per-tenant state machine. Also validate prometheus histogram mapping and that histogram sum/count semantics are preserved when exported via remote_write.
